requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.subtitle: Ticket intent and acceptance criteria
requirements.description: The ticket — Jira ND-* or a local id — carries the acceptance criteria and intent that /design actually reads first, /dev checks its own work against directly, and hand-off verifies evidence against. One ticket, read at every stage.
details: Read first by /design
Read again by /dev
Verified against when /dev reports back
requirements.markdown:
# Requirements

- Ticket intent and acceptance criteria
- Constraints
- What "done" means

tracker.title: Task tracking system
tracker.subtitle: Source of intent & execution tasks
tracker.description: Jira project ND, per this repo's own conventions — the ticket's home. Holds the requirements /design reads first, receives the implementation tasks /design hands back, and is where /dev reports its result and triggers whatever the ticket's workflow runs next.
details: Holds the ticket's requirements
Receives /design's implementation tasks
Receives /dev's result report
Triggers the next stage on transition
tracker.markdown:
# Task tracking system

- Jira project ND
- Requirements (the ticket itself)
- Implementation tasks
- Status transitions

design.title: /design
design.subtitle: Context → Frame → Research → Evaluate → Solution → Publish
design.description: Explores the requirements and existing architecture, drafts and evaluates options, and — once a recommendation is approved — publishes the settled decision into the HLD and hands implementation tasks back to the tracker.
details: Produces its own interim working drafts first
Only the settled recommendation graduates
Rationale and rejected options never graduate
Hands implementation tasks back to the tracker
design.markdown:
# /design

1. Frame the problem
2. Research options
3. Evaluate and recommend
4. Publish the approved solution
5. Create implementation tasks

hitl.title: HITL
hitl.subtitle: Human reviews and approves the draft
hitl.description: The Review Gate stage of /design: a human validates the drafted solution — checked against the WAF — before anything is allowed to publish into the HLD.
details: Validates the solution drafted in History
Approves before /design can publish
The one human checkpoint before a permanent record changes
hitl.markdown:
# HITL

- Reviews the drafted solution
- Approves, or sends it back to Address Feedback

target.title: Target State (HLD)
target.subtitle: Permanent — aspirational design intent
target.description: WHY and WHAT a project is designed toward. Holds only settled, per-container architecture descriptions — not the drafts, options, or rationale that produced them. Those stay behind in History as the Story’s own ledger.
details: Populated by /design’s settled solution
Governs the next stage, /dev
Updated again only on an authorized deviation
target.markdown:
# Target State (HLD)

- Containers/ — one settled architecture doc per container

hld-container.title: Containers/ (per-container architecture)
hld-container.subtitle: What the HLD actually holds
hld-container.description: One settled architecture doc per container — what it is and why, not the options that were considered or rejected to get there.
details: One file per container
Populated once /design’s solution is approved
Read directly by /dev
hld-container.markdown:
# Containers/

- Web Explorer.md
- Web Docs.md
- Web Portal.md
- …

dev.title: /dev
dev.subtitle: Context → Plan → Implement → Test → Document → Completion
dev.description: Reads the requirements and the HLD as source of truth, accounts for the current LLD before touching anything, then builds. Produces code and its own interim working notes the whole time, and verifies against requirements before reporting back.
details: Governed by the HLD, not improvising
Accounts for current LLD components before changing them
Produces its own interim state (Stories/impl/) and code
An authorized deviation is the one path back into the HLD
Verifies against requirements before reporting to the tracker
dev.markdown:
# /dev

1. Read HLD + LLD + requirements
2. Plan the steps
3. Implement, verified step by step
4. Document — updates LLD, surfaces any deviation
5. Complete — report result to the tracker

current.title: Current State (LLD)
current.subtitle: Permanent — current implementation detail
current.description: WHAT is currently built and HOW it works — descriptive, not aspirational. /dev's interim notes populate this on essentially every ticket that changes a container's implementation detail.
details: Populated by /dev’s interim implementation notes
Governs the next /dev ticket that touches this component
A gap vs. the HLD is a delivery gap by design, not an error
current.markdown:
# Current State (LLD)

- Container docs — what’s actually built
- Component contracts, interfaces, dependencies

component.title: Container docs
component.subtitle: As-built, per container
component.description: One doc per container, describing actual responsibilities, dependencies, and interfaces — not intent.
details: Real component boundaries
Updated by /dev document
Read by the next ticket that touches this container
component.markdown:
# Container doc

- Responsibilities
- Interfaces and dependencies
- Current behavior

history.title: History State (Stories)
history.subtitle: Interim — the ticket’s own point-in-time ledger
history.description: One Story folder per ticket, holding design/, solution/, and impl/ as siblings — every draft, option, and working note either lifecycle produces. Archived read-only once the ticket completes, never reopened to add a doc.
details: design/ and solution/ are /design’s own drafts, not duplicated into the HLD
impl/ is /dev’s own drafts, not duplicated into the LLD
Populates the permanent records once settled
history.markdown:
# Stories/[TICKET]/

- design/ — Frame, Research, Evaluate
- solution/ — Architecture, Design, Stack, Efforts
- impl/ — intent, plan, report

hld-design.title: design/ (Frame · Research · Evaluate)
hld-design.subtitle: /design’s own working drafts
hld-design.description: The interim working drafts that produced the HLD's settled decision — kept as the Story's own history, not duplicated into the permanent doc.
details: Frames the problem
Compares options with no recommendation yet
Recommends one, with a WAF check

hld-solution.title: solution/ (Architecture · Design · Stack · Efforts)
hld-solution.subtitle: What actually populates the HLD
hld-solution.description: The certainty artifacts — immutable after the Publish gate. This is what /design actually publishes into the HLD, and what /dev later reads as its source of truth.
details: The approved architecture, design, stack, and effort estimate
Reviewed before publish
Read directly by /dev

notes.title: impl/ (Intent · Plan · Report)
notes.subtitle: /dev’s own working drafts
notes.description: What ran, what was found, and how long it took — updated every step of /dev, not written after the fact.
details: Updated by every step, not just at the end
Records review findings and tech debt
Preserves history without replacing the LLD

code.title: Code
code.subtitle: Verified, step by step
code.description: The actual change — built and verified one step at a time, each with its own observed check before moving on.
details: Built against the HLD, not improvised
Verified per step, not only at the end
Not a substitute for the LLD
code.markdown:
# Code

- Implemented behavior
- Build, lint, typecheck per step
- Acceptance-criteria evidence

handoff.title: Next stage
handoff.subtitle: Deployment · testing
handoff.description: Whatever the ticket's own workflow runs after hand-off — deployment, testing, release — kicked off once the tracker sees /dev's result and transitions the ticket. Outside this harness's own lifecycle.
details: Triggered by the tracker, not by /dev directly
Scope depends on the ticket's own workflow
Outside this harness's own lifecycle
handoff.markdown:
# Next stage

- Deployment
- Testing
- Release — whatever the ticket's own workflow defines
